useReactiveState()

The useReactiveState() method connects an active Vue effect scope to the State of a and returns its current Snapshot as a readonly reactive object.

This method is available only for Vue and extends the contract with a reactive State surface for Vue components.

Vue Package

The Vue Extension is available from the /vue package on npm. 

{{`npm install @sdux-vault/vue`}}

Download /vue from npm →

Usage

Use useReactiveState() when a Vue component renders State. It returns the current Snapshot and keeps its fields reactive for subsequent State changes.

Choose the State access surface
Surface Usage Result
useReactiveState() Render State in a Vue component Returns a readonly reactive Snapshot and connects the active effect scope to future State changes.
state Read State outside an effect scope Returns the latest Snapshot synchronously without creating a subscription.
state$ Observe every State emission Provides an Observable for consumers that explicitly manage a subscription and its cleanup.
Do not rely on later updates to validate the initial component State
  1. Initial setup: A manual state$ subscription created after the has initialized can miss the earlier emission that committed initialState.
  2. Later updates: A subsequent replaceState() or mergeState() emission can reach that subscription, even though the initial component State was absent.
  3. Vue State surface: Use useReactiveState() so the component receives the current Snapshot and remains connected to subsequent State changes through the same effect-scope contract.

Before component setup

The must already be initialized by the application's State setup. Import its stable reference into the Vue component instead of creating or initializing it inside component setup.

During setup

  1. Call useReactiveState() within an active Vue effect scope, including a component's setup context.
  2. Store the returned readonly reactive Snapshot in a stable component reference.
  3. Read hasValue, value, isLoading, and error from that Snapshot to determine what the component displays.

When State changes

When the commits new State, the returned Snapshot exposes the latest committed fields reactively. The component does not require a separate state$ subscription for this State surface.

When the effect scope is disposed

The State subscription belongs to the Vue effect scope created by the consumer of useReactiveState(). Disposing that scope also disposes its State subscription, so the component does not perform manual subscription cleanup.

Event handlers and code outside an effect scope

Use state when an event handler or other imperative code needs the latest Snapshot at the moment that code runs. Use state$ when every State emission is required outside the Vue effect scope, and dispose of that Observable subscription when its owner is no longer active.

Render State with one reactive surface

For Vue component State, use useReactiveState() as the reactive surface. Reading state does not connect the component to future State changes, while using state$ creates a separate subscription lifecycle that the component must manage.

Method Contract
Runtime Invocation
Method Description
useReactiveState<T>

inputs:

  • None

return:

  • Readonly<StateSnapshotShape<T>>
Subscribes the active Vue effect scope to State updates and returns the latest committed Snapshot as a readonly reactive object.
Snapshot Output

The returned readonly reactive Snapshot represents the latest committed State for the .

Example

This component imports an existing, initialized and calls useReactiveState() during setup. The template reads each Snapshot field directly from the returned readonly reactive object. 

{{`<script setup lang="ts">
import { exampleCell } from './example.cell';

const snapshot = exampleCell.useReactiveState();
</script>

<template>
  <p v-if="snapshot.isLoading">Loading...</p>
  <p v-else-if="snapshot.error" role="alert" v-text="snapshot.error.message"></p>
  <p v-else-if="!snapshot.hasValue">No State is available.</p>
  <pre v-else v-text="JSON.stringify(snapshot.value, null, 2)"></pre>
</template>`}}
